text: Migrations are applied once per deploy, before any instance of the new release starts. They are additive only, so the live release keeps working. Drops and renames wait for a later release, after the release that uses them has been retired.
A failed migration stops the deploy: the new release is never started and the live colour keeps serving.

There is a gate before user traffic: every instance passes /healthz 3 times in a row (10 s apart) and the smoke suite passes, within 10 minutes of the instances starting. Otherwise the deploy aborts without touching the public listener.
Traffic is switched in one step by repointing the public listener to the new colour's target group, with no gradual shift.
For 15 minutes after the switch, the 5xx rate is watched. Above 1% over any 5-minute window, an automatic rollback points the listener back at the old colour. A rollback never reverses migrations.

The old colour stays running, untouched, for 30 minutes after the switch. Until then, a rollback (automatic, or started by an engineer as a pipeline job) points the listener back at it. After it is shut down, any rollback is a normal deploy of the previous release.

The deploy is written as a Markdown checklist of steps in the order they are done, from the merge to the end of the deploy. Each step says what starts it, what it changes and what happens if it fails.
The artifact says where deploy state is kept, including which colour is live and the times that later steps count from.
